about: The evangelium of the formulary “Second Sunday after Epiphany” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: At that time there was a marriage in Cana of Galilee, and the Mother of Jesus was there. Jesus also and His disciples were invited to the marriage. When the wine failed, the Mother of Jesus said unto Him: They have no wine. Jesus said unto her: What is that to Me and to thee, Woman? Mine hour is not yet come. His Mother said unto the servants: Whatsoever He shall say unto you, do ye. Now there were set there six stone waterpots, according to the manner of the purifying of the Jews, containing two or three measures apiece. Jesus said unto them: Fill the waterpots with water. They filled them up to the brim. He said unto them: Draw out now and bear unto the chief steward of the feast. And they bore it. When the chief steward had tasted the water made wine and knew not whence it was, though the servants who had drawn the water knew, he called the bridegroom and said unto him: Every man at first setteth forth good wine, and when men have drunk freely, then that which is worse; but thou hast kept the good wine until now. This beginning of signs did Jesus in Cana of Galilee; He manifested His glory, and His disciples believed in Him.
